name: Jehoram
overview: Jehoram was a male king from the tribe of Judah, known as the son of Jehoshaphat and ruler of Judah. He was married to Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab, and he committed evil in the sight of the LORD. His reign was marked by significant spiritual decline due to his actions and alliances.
namesAndTitles: Jehoram's name means 'YHWH exalts,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names, though it was not given by God. He is also referred to as Joram, meaning 'YHWH is exalted,' and by various royal titles such as King of Judah, King Joram, and King Jehoram, indicating his position as monarch of Judah.
familyAndRelationships: Jehoram was the son of Jehoshaphat and the husband of Athaliah, Ahab's daughter. He was likely the father of Ahaziah and Jehosheba. His death was caused by individuals named Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azaryahu, Michael, and Sephatiah, who acted as his killers.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoram's reign exemplifies the consequences of forsaking God's ways through ungodly alliances and personal evil. His marriage to Athaliah led him to walk in the evil practices of Israel's kings, resulting in idolatry and violence, including the killing of his brothers to secure his throne. His leadership brought spiritual devastation to Judah, culminating in a painful death that went unmourned, underscoring the destructive impact of disobedience to God.
